prompt: I need a first usable set of product requirements for replacing our paper field-inspection process with a tablet app. This is for the PM taking the work into delivery, so cover field capture, the first release boundary, records, safety, and unresolved decisions. Read the material in this folder and keep the requirements concrete without making up facts. Put the result at docs/requirements.md. End the file with a ```json block of the form {"requirements": [{"id": "R1", "text": "..."}], "assumptions": ["..."]}.

facts.answer: Most routes lose connectivity for up to 8 hours, so the app must support 8 hours of offline work and queue submissions and photos until it reconnects.
There are 12 rugged tablets shared across crews. At sign-out, a worker must choose the tablet's asset tag, and the app must not require a personal device.
Attach at most 4 photos per inspection item, keep the original resolution, and warn or block before capturing identifiable people or vehicle plates.
If two tablets edit the same inspection while offline, keep both versions and flag the record for field-lead resolution; never silently overwrite either submission.
An inspection is not complete until the inspector attests on the tablet and the field lead approves it within 2 business days. The lead's approval is the export gate.
Stop the inspection and notify the field lead for any chlorine smell, exposed electrical conductor, or unstable ground. The app must offer a safety-stop status without requiring a reading or photo.

scriptedUser.defaultReply: I'm not sure, use your judgement.

rubric.criterion: Requirements separate confirmed operating rules from decisions that still need an owner and do not turn the old draft into settled policy. Fail: rules from the old draft are written as confirmed, or open decisions have no owner. Partial: confirmed and open items are separated, but only some confirmed rules appear (8 hours offline with queued submissions and photos, 12 shared tablets chosen by asset tag at sign-out, at most 4 photos per item at original resolution, both versions kept when two tablets edit one inspection, tablet attestation then field-lead approval within 2 business days as the export gate), or open decisions have no owner. Pass: all of these appear as confirmed requirements, the records retention rule and the managed tablet boundary are kept, and each decision still open names who must decide it, with nothing taken from the old draft as policy. (code cannot check this because it requires judging the source evidence and the document's interpretation)

The requirements are practical for a field crew and preserve the intent of the paper process without adding needless workflow burden. Fail: it adds steps the paper process never had, or omits the safety stop. Partial: it keeps the capture steps, but forces a reading or photo before a safety stop, or loses the paper-form not-applicable meaning. Pass: it offers a safety-stop status (chlorine smell, exposed electrical conductor, unstable ground) that needs no reading or photo and notifies the field lead, keeps the paper-form not-applicable semantics, warns or blocks before photographing identifiable people or vehicle plates, and adds no step beyond what the folder asks for. (code cannot check this because usability and proportionality require human review)

The final message says plainly what was delivered, what was assumed and what is still open, without claiming more than the files show. Fail: the message says the work is complete or settled while the decisions it lists as needing an owner and the points taken from the old draft stay unmentioned, or it does not say that docs/requirements.md was written. Partial: it names docs/requirements.md and what it holds, but lists no assumptions, or leaves out the decisions it lists as needing an owner and the points taken from the old draft. Pass: it names docs/requirements.md and its closing JSON block, lists the assumptions made, says the decisions it lists as needing an owner and the points taken from the old draft still need an answer or a check, and claims nothing the files do not show. (code cannot check this because the message is free text about the work)

verdicts.note: The prompt specifies the desired outcome (requirements document covering listed topics) and output format, but does not prescribe methods, frameworks, or processes.

The prompt, fixture materials, and hidden tests align: fixture provides partial context, tests check for specific values unlocked only by asking the scripted user. A competent person would know to gather requirements from available materials and clarify gaps through questions.

Critical numeric values (8 hours offline, 12 tablets, 4 photos, 2 business days, specific safety hazards) exist only in scripted facts. Fixture establishes that older drafts and notes are not approved, preventing a quick copy-paste answer.

All six facts have natural topic labels matching how a person would ask (offline/connectivity, tablets/handoff, photos/privacy, conflicting edits, inspection completion, safety stop). Reference scores 100/100.
Fixture contains no scripted facts, only context that points to gaps. Prompt mentions topic areas but does not reveal specific values. ASKS.json is in solution/, not visible to agent.

items.note: Prompt asks to read material and create concrete requirements, no specific method prescribed.
Fixture contains paper process, asset catalog, operating notes but not synthesized requirements.
Hidden tests check patterns matching scripted facts; rubric aligns with prompt and fixture.
Competent PM could create requirements from fixture; different implementation would pass if captures essentials.
